primary_category.subcategory: A2.4 Information search, retrieval, gathering, and evaluation

evidence.quote: the transcript alone doesn't tell us enough, so we pull in a diagnostic test, maybe an observation, and go from there
evidence.explanation: The worker actively seeks additional evidence when existing records are insufficient, a core information-gathering act.

evidence.quote: So by the deadline I had four numbers in front of me.
evidence.explanation: The worker collects, tracks, and consolidates multiple evidence sources (transcript, diagnostic, quiz, self-report) before acting, a direct instance of gathering and evaluating information.

evidence.quote: the counselor couldn't verify their grading scale or how rigorous that course actually was
evidence.explanation: The worker attempts to verify the reliability of an external record, a core evaluative information task.

evidence.quote: I converted everything to the same 100-point scale and averaged the four together. That gave me a composite right around 79
evidence.explanation: The worker performs scale conversion and arithmetic averaging of numerical evidence to produce a quantitative placement score.

evidence.quote: So I asked my chair if we could hold off a few days and get a diagnostic test done, plus sit him in on one of my classes
evidence.explanation: The worker designs a non-routine evidence-gathering plan (sequencing diagnostic testing and observation) to resolve an ambiguous placement problem within a fixed deadline.

evidence.quote: I chose the second option and set up twice-weekly tutoring.
evidence.explanation: The worker devises and implements an intervention plan in response to an unexpected performance signal, weighing costs and benefits of alternatives.

evidence.quote: I've seen transfer students hit a rough patch adjusting to a new teacher's style and pacing before leveling out
evidence.explanation: The worker applies a generalized mental model derived from prior experience to interpret a new, ambiguous case.

evidence.quote: The counselor coordinates logistics, but the placement call is mine, with my chair signing off.
evidence.explanation: The worker holds decision authority within a multi-stakeholder process involving a counselor, department chair, and parent, and must align these roles toward a placement outcome.

evidence.quote: The counselor also flagged that switching tracks mid-year could complicate his transcript. Combined with the parent's request, keeping him in with continued support seemed like the right call.
evidence.explanation: The worker integrates input from multiple stakeholders (counselor, parent) into a coordinated decision.

evidence.quote: I chose the second option and set up twice-weekly tutoring.
evidence.explanation: The worker arranges instructional support (tutoring) intended to develop the student's skills, a coaching-oriented action, though direct tutoring delivery is not described in detail.

all_observed_categories: A2.4 Information search, retrieval, gathering, and evaluation
not_observed_or_insufficient: A1.1 Strength - no physical exertion described
A1.2 Dexterity - no fine motor or instrument manipulation described
A1.3 Navigation - no physical movement through space described as task-relevant

A2.1 Uncodified visual/auditory processing - the classroom observation involves informal impression-forming, but the interview does not describe perceptual pattern recognition in sufficient sensory detail to independently support this category
A3.1 Serving and attending - the relationship with the student is placement-oriented rather than an immediate service-response interaction
A3.3 Selling and influencing - no persuasion or negotiation with the parent, chair, or student is described; the chair 'signs off' but no negotiation is evidenced
A3.5 Caring - no explicit emotional or welfare-centered support is detailed, though confidence/well-being is mentioned briefly
ambiguities: A2.2 Literacy is plausibly involved (transcript reading, parent's written request) but is not elaborated as a meaningful task in itself; it is treated as embedded within A2.4 rather than a standalone primary/secondary category.

The classroom sit-in and quiz observation could support A2.1 (uncodified perceptual judgment of how the student handled a live assessment), but the interview describes it only in terms of the resulting quiz score, not perceptual interpretation, so it was not assigned independently.

evidence.quote: I'm usually the one who handles course placement questions when a student transfers in mid-year, since I know the sequencing best.
evidence.explanation: The worker is the designated decision-maker for the placement judgment and chooses which evidence to gather and how to combine it.

evidence.quote: the placement call is mine, with my chair signing off
evidence.explanation: The teacher's decision requires approval from a department chair, indicating a review layer, though the teacher retains substantive decision control.

evidence.quote: So I asked my chair if we could hold off a few days... She agreed.
evidence.explanation: The teacher coordinates with the chair and counselor at multiple points, though the core evidence-integration and judgment work is performed individually.

evidence.quote: It varies. Sometimes the transcript is solid and we just slot them in. Other times... we pull in a diagnostic test, maybe an observation
evidence.explanation: Placement decisions recur but vary in complexity depending on transcript clarity, indicating semi-recurring but non-identical tasks.

evidence.quote: our department's cutoff of 75 for Algebra II placement
evidence.explanation: A cutoff exists (some standardization), but the method for reaching the composite score itself is not a prescribed departmental procedure ('I converted everything... and averaged').

evidence.quote: the school wasn't one I recognized, and the counselor couldn't verify their grading scale or how rigorous that course actually was
evidence.explanation: Key inputs to the decision (transcript meaning, grading comparability) are explicitly uncertain.

evidence.quote: the transcript alone doesn't tell us enough... a few weeks in, he scored 55 on his first unit test, below the class median
evidence.explanation: The worker must respond to an atypical incomplete record and later an unexpected poor test result, both requiring situational adaptation rather than routine procedure.

tools.role_in_task: Recording, converting, and tracking numerical scores (transcript GPA conversion, composite calculation) and administering a written self-assessment survey

evidence.quote: I converted everything to the same 100-point scale and averaged the four together
evidence.explanation: Score conversion and averaging strongly implies use of basic office/computing tools (e.g., spreadsheet or calculator), though no specific software is named.

task_anchors.task_description: Evaluating an ambiguous out-of-state transcript and deciding to delay placement pending additional evidence
Converting four heterogeneous evidence sources to a common scale and averaging them into a composite placement score
Interpreting a poor unit-test result in context and designing a support intervention rather than immediate reassignment
Integrating performance trend, counselor input, and parent request into a final quarter-end retention decision
